answer: A harbor lease model makes identity a measured circuit, not a key. Every agent must hold a wharf slot: a distinct network path whose round-trip latency is probed every few minutes by rotating third parties, and whose bandwidth floor is checked at settlement. Slots are priced per path, not per account, so a thousand aliases on one uplink share a single congestion curve and collapse into a tundra of missed probes. Honest agents pay one lease; a farm pays one per genuinely separate path, which is the cost it cannot fake. Duplicate paths are merged and their bonds burned.
